correctness.rationale: Orthogonal four-mode decomposition produces the exact quartic; its squared-root signs produce one real and one imaginary pair when ηγ>0. All zero modes are invariant dark eigenvectors, so growth is Θ(e^{µt}). At η=0 the critical trimer cube vanishes while square does not, yielding Θ(t²). Direct expansion of the negative squared-eigenvalue root yields the claimed linear, square-root and crossover limits. Bundled independent full-matrix numerical checks and symbolic determinant passed; finite tests only corroborate the proof.

originality.rationale: The finite trimer threshold and the qualitative generic thresholdless mechanism are explicitly established prior work, so neither is treated as a new isolated statement. The verified primary texts instead concern a three-site oligomer, generic degenerate wave equations, photonic arrays with different couplings, and bipartite matrices with whole-part gain/loss. The proposed all-size one-pair weighted-bipartite quartic, its exact exponential growth exponent, and a singular coupling/gain double scaling are not direct specializations of statements inspected in those sources. Remaining risk is a general spectral theorem or prior targeted graph calculation implying these exact expressions. The 2017 passive-dimer bridge study is a plausible near-overlap, with only a preview accessible: its topology differs but exact implication remains a material residual risk.
residual_risks: Highly relevant Teimourpour–Özdemir–El-Ganainy (2017) passive-bridge study could not be inspected past the first-page publisher preview; its uninspected equations could provide stronger coverage or imply parts of the theorem.
Broader spectral perturbation and PT-degenerate-mode theory might imply the quantified root crossover by specialization.
Historical photonic graph computations or inaccessible full texts may already contain the exact one-pair weighted bipartite polynomial.
No search or publication index is exhaustive; independent literature and mathematics review remains outstanding.

value.rationale: The theorem quantifies how arbitrarily weak passive-edge coupling destroys the otherwise finite unbroken PT phase, including exact exponential growth and a parameter-dependent singular transition in exponent at an exceptional point. The all-size, weighted graph result gives a meaningful stability diagnostic and connection-multiplicity scaling for gain–loss networks; the value does not rest solely on the generic known fact of thresholdless breaking.
